correctness.rationale: For every law with mass strictly on each side of 1/2, conditional independent Poisson survival gives S_B=e^{-B/2}Phi(x-y); Phi is strictly convex, and its derivative tends to opposite signs at the two infinities, hence a unique real minimizer. Clipping to [-B,B] proves all budgets, derivative at zero gives correct mean-sign orientation, and positive-part boundaries follow. Worst-case over all laws is the maximum of two endpoint survival rates; equal exposure uniquely minimizes it. Beta endpoint Laplace analysis proves both polynomial asymptotics, while clipping makes the mixed optimum exactly exponential for all B>|z*|. Direct two-class example certifies sharp activation. The embedded standalone checker passed 17855 numerical/exact-rational supplementary assertions; these finite checks are not treated as universal proof.

value.rationale: Persistent low-trappability survivor tails make removal costly in the motivating experiments. For the nontrivial complementary-lure class, the theorem supplies a sharp distribution-dependent intervention threshold, universal invariant effort difference after activation, exact minimax protection without identifying the trait law, and a qualitative polynomial-to-exponential survival-tail change under beta heterogeneity. These are natural operational boundaries rather than an unmotivated arbitrary calculation. The result is conditional theory, not a field prescription.
